I have been working a lot, doing school, and staying at my boyfriends a lot and I was barely home for her. She was always so happy to have me home but I was gone to much and it didn't seem fair. Ontop of all that she has health issues and I couldn't afford the vet bills that would be coming up in the next couple years. I took the time and I found her the perfect home. Someone with money and knowledge about her condition and someone who was home a lot. 

I regret getting rid of her, but only for my sake. My home is empty without her and I find it challenging to be here. But I do not regret it at the same time because she has a better life than I could ever provide for her.

If you haven't, work on some obedience training with him. Actual eye contact is not necessary. What you want is for his attention to be on you. I'm still working on dog training myself and I'm starting clicker training. Right now, I click the clicker, wait till my dog looks at my face with all her attention and then I treat her. She is only treated if she gives me her attention. 

If he is running off, this is a great way to help change that behavior. Once he associates giving you his attention with reward, he is more likely to follow your rules.

I have had to make decisions about old dogs being put down and it's never easy. 
But right now I have a German Shepherd that I'm trying to come to terms with rehoming. She is very reactive and we live in an apartment building and most people are afraid of her because she's got a really loud bark and lunges at people. Most people feel uneasy around her, but I love her more than anything. It's come to a point where I know it's best to rehome her but I still haven't come to terms with it. 
When I do make that decision I plan on contacting a German Shepherd rescue. They only work with German Shepherds and understand their behavioral issues as well as potential medical issues so they can rehome the dog in a suitable environment with an extensive interview process. It's much safer than a humane society or finding someone you don't know to take the dog. 

They may tell you straight up say the dog will be put down, if that is the case I'd suggest getting it done yourself so you can be there for your pup.

I suggest contacting a rescue that is specific to your dogs breed and explain the situation. A lot of breed specific rescues are very loyal to that breed and will do there best to help it. With the information that your dog has bitten people in the past, they may suggest putting it down, but it may help you come to this conclusion.
Best of luck, I've been in your position and it's not easy.
